proof_summary: Writing each prime-power binomial step as the previous coefficient times \(\prod_{(i,p)=1}(1+mq/i)\), with \(q=p^r\), and pairing \(i\) with \(q-i\) reduces the needed comparison to reciprocal-square sums: these give \(U^2-1=6q^2T\) and \(V-1=q^2T\), with enough divisibility of \(T\); at \(r=2\), the otherwise surviving quadratic product term vanishes by an elementary-symmetric cancellation among lifted unit classes. The remaining coefficient vanishes modulo \(p^3\) for \(p\ge5\) from the residues \(\binom{3p^s}{p^s}\equiv3\), \(\binom{2p^s}{p^s}\equiv2\), while for \(p=3\) the stable residues \(84,20\pmod{3^5}\) combine with a unit-class lifting argument for \(T\); the lone \(p=3,r=2\) case is settled by direct finite computation.
